staticMarkdownSelectors.target: Strokes: 2 · Key (radical): 刀 (no. 18) · JLPT: N1 (community list)

刀 concerns swords and blades. The standalone word 刀 かたな means a sword, especially a Japanese single-edged sword. The character's wider cutting-tool senses do not make かたな a general word for every knife.

Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology: Picture a blade inside the bent, hooked outline, with the separate sweeping stroke starting inside it. This is a memory aid for the modern shape, not a reconstruction of its history.
トウ
日本刀 にほんとう — Japanese sword; also read にっぽんとう
かたな
刀 かたな — sword; katana
そり
KANJIDIC2 lists this reading; no independently allocated word example is established here

剃刀 かみそり means "razor," usually written in kana. It has a special whole-word reading: the kana ending そり is not by itself evidence that 刀 independently supplies that reading. Keep the source reading そり for lookup, not as a new standalone word for "razor."
刀 かたな — sword; katana
日本刀 にほんとう — Japanese sword
剃刀 かみそり — razor; recognize the kanji spelling, but the word is usually written in kana
Compare 力, "power." In 力 the slanting stroke crosses the upper stroke; in 刀 it starts inside the hooked outline. Both have two strokes.
乃, with connecting or particle-related uses, 凹, "concave; sunken," and 凸, "convex; protruding," do not share 刀's sword/blade meaning.
Learn each whole word with its reading. The とう-only scalpel and engraving-tool senses in the standalone 刀 dictionary family do not automatically belong to かたな.
Metadata: KANJIDIC2, 2026-11-02 snapshot. Word families: JMdict, entries 1446420, 1464780 and 1435180. Character and lexical readings: Digital Daijisen, 刀 and 日本刀.
日本刀 にほんとう — Japanese sword
日本刀 is a Japanese sword made in the traditional Japanese manner. It is a noun naming the object, not an action. The dictionary also records the reading にっぽんとう.
博物館で古い日本刀を見ました。 (はくぶつかんでふるいにほんとうをみました。) — I saw an old Japanese sword at the museum.
これは日本刀の写真です。 (これはにほんとうのしゃしんです。) — This is a photograph of a Japanese sword.
In 日本刀を見る (にほんとうをみる), "look at a Japanese sword," を marks the object. 日本刀の写真 uses の to connect the sword with its photograph.

日 and 本 together spell the country name 日本 (にほん／にっぽん), "Japan." Here 日本 modifies 刀, read トウ and meaning "sword": a Japanese sword. Treat 日本 as the country name, not as a new literal "sun + book" definition.
The whole compound is にほんとう or にっぽんとう. The two readings name the same category; learn them as documented forms, not as a general rule for changing sounds in other compounds.
刀 かたな, "sword; katana," overlaps with 日本刀. A katana is a familiar example of a Japanese sword, but 日本刀 is not limited to one narrowly defined historical subtype.
ナイフ, "knife," 包丁 ほうちょう, "kitchen knife," and 剃刀 かみそり, "razor," name different kinds of cutting tools. They are not general substitutes for 日本刀. There is no natural lexical antonym.

日本刀 identifies a Japanese sword tradition, not simply any knife made in Japan. The category is often associated with a curved, single-edged sword, but do not turn that familiar image into a rule that every 日本刀 must have exactly the same shape.
Dictionary: JMdict, entry 1464780, both readings; Digital Daijisen and Seisenban Nihon Kokugo Daijiten, 日本刀.

日本刀 にほんとう — Japanese sword; 日本 names Japan in this compound

日 and 本 together spell the country name 日本 (にほん／にっぽん), "Japan." Here 日本 modifies 刀, read トウ and meaning "sword": a Japanese sword. Treat 日本 as the country name, not as a new literal "sun + book" definition.
日本刀 にほんとう — Japanese sword; 日本 names Japan in this compound
刀 かたな — sword; katana

刀 is one character, with the native reading かたな for this standalone word. There is no compound to split. The character also has the on reading トウ, but another reading does not make all dictionary senses interchangeable.
剃刀 かみそり — razor; recognize the kanji spelling, but the word is usually written in kana

剃 concerns shaving and 刀 a blade, which helps associate the spelling with a shaving tool. The assigned かみそり is a special whole-word reading: do not split it into invented independent readings for 剃 and 刀.
